summary: What a number is counted in, such as percent, hours or tonnes.
example: Hours, as in the hours between produce arriving at a depot and being collected.
definition: What a measure is counted in, declared once so one quantity is not spelled several ways. A standard set ships with every vault (percent, count, ratio, score, index, days, hours, months), and an organisation declares its own beside them in the same way, such as a currency or a scale it defined. A unit carries its dimension from a closed set (percent, count, money, ratio, duration), so what a unit is called and what kind of quantity it is stay separate: hours and days are both durations. A unit is not what is counted (deliveries, members), which is said in the KPI's definition, not a KPI, and not a data source.

/spec/dimension.guide: What kind of quantity this is: percent (a share out of a hundred), count, money, ratio (one quantity over another, or a number on a defined scale) or duration. It tells anything adding two measures whether it may.

poor.text: percent, for a produce grade scored out of 100
poor.why: A score on a scale is not a share of a whole: it is a ratio, like the shipped Score.

/spec/symbol.guide: The short form, where there is one, such as % for percent or hrs for hours. Leave it empty when the unit is written out.

/spec/description.guide: What exactly is counted, where the name alone could be read two ways: rounding, which currency, what the scale runs from and to.
good: United States dollars, which is what the cooperative settles member payments in.
Hours, to the nearest hour unless the KPI says otherwise.

poor.why: Repeats the dimension and does not say which currency.

/metadata/name.guide: The name, as people say it and as lists show it.

KPI:/spec/unit.ask: Which KPIs are counted in this unit?
KPI:/spec/unit.ifNone: Nothing has to be defined first: a unit stands on its own, and a KPI picks it when its definition is written.
